audit_findings.title: Recurring capitalized IP-defense spending may be stripped from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $26.903 million computed LTM upper bound for non-Helimix/other intangible additions; exact recurring IP-defense subset unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Recurring capitalized defense cash spending must enter maintenance reinvestment in OE; adding back its amortization without deducting the additions inflates the anchor and every scenario.
audit_findings.evidence: Capitalized costs incurred during 2025, 2024, and 2023 primarily relate to external legal costs incurred in the defense of our patents and trademarks, net of settlements received.
audit_findings.explanation: The recurring capitalization is demonstrated, but its omission from OE is not. The computed LTM upper bound is 23.3% of the $115.6 million anchor, large enough to alter the valuation range materially.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile intangible-addition ledgers through July 4, 2026, identify defense costs net of settlements, confirm amounts already deducted, and rerun OE after deducting only recurring maintenance defense spending.

audit_findings.title: Helimix acquisition spending may be mismatched with the null perimeter
audit_findings.magnitude: $38.0 million filed cash payment, equal to 32.9% of anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: The acquisition payment can depress anchor OE if treated as maintenance reinvestment; excluding it while inconsistently handling acquired operations can inflate OE or growth expectations.
audit_findings.evidence: During the third quarter of 2025, we acquired certain assets, including designs, tooling, and intellectual property, related to the Helimix branded shaker bottle for $ 38.0 million in cash.
audit_findings.explanation: The payment and acquired assets are demonstrated, but the alleged perimeter mismatch is unresolved. At nearly one-third of anchor OE, either treatment error could materially move the valuation outputs.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $35.6 million of acquired intangibles and $2.4 million of tooling through the LTM OE bridge, identify acquired earnings included in each period, establish a consistent consolidated perimeter, and rerun both consistent treatments.

audit_findings.title: Supplier finance obligations can evade the debt bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $90.3 million filed balance at July 4, 2026; $36.3 million computed increase from $54.0 million at January 3, 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Because SFP obligations sit in accounts payable, their increase can boost operating cash flow and OE through working capital without appearing as debt; a later unwind reverses that benefit.
audit_findings.evidence: The outstanding payment obligations under the SFP recorded within accounts payable in our consolidated balance sheets at January 3, 2026 and December 28, 2024 were $ 54.0 million and $ 63.1 million, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The classification and $36.3 million increase are demonstrated; failure to normalize or capture them is unresolved. The increase equals 31.4% of anchor OE and is reasonably capable of materially inflating the current numerator. Merely omitting it from a context-only debt bridge would not itself change value.
audit_findings.action: Isolate SFP movements from accounts-payable cash flows for every OE year, determine the sustainable supplier-finance level, rerun OE with normalized working capital, and avoid a separate deduction if the burden is already fully captured.

audit_findings.title: Unrealized intercompany FX gain may remain in the anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $7.167 million filed FY2025 other income; $0.108 million computed LTM total other income
audit_findings.mechanism: Any unpurged unrealized FX gain raises after-tax OE; historical inconsistencies can also distort trend calculations.
audit_findings.evidence: The change versus the prior year period was primarily due to unrealized foreign currency gains on intercompany balances in the current period versus unrealized foreign currency losses on intercompany balances in the prior year.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that FY2025 other income was primarily unrealized intercompany FX, but retention in OE is unresolved. Even treating the entire $7.167 million pretax balance as OE would be only 6.2% of the anchor and would reduce bull value by about $1.57 per share, leaving it near $24.50 versus the $40.82 price. The computed LTM total other-income balance is only $0.108 million.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the OE bridge purges intercompany FX gains and losses consistently from the anchor and history; correct the series if needed, but no conclusion-changing rerun is indicated by the available scale.

audit_findings.title: The stated share ceiling may not cover above-target performance awards
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified (242,000-share H1 2026 performance adjustment is filed, equal to 0.32% of the stated denominator)
audit_findings.mechanism: Additional above-target PRSUs increase the fully diluted share denominator and reduce intrinsic value per share.
audit_findings.evidence: Represents additional performance-based awards issued as a result of the achievement of actual performance results above the performance targets at grant date.
audit_findings.explanation: Above-target issuance is demonstrated, but the maximum payout and any shares missing from the 75.790796 million denominator are not disclosed in the supplied record. The observed adjustment is small, but it does not establish an upper bound, so materiality remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the governing PRSU agreements and award schedules, calculate maximum earned shares for every outstanding grant, reconcile them to the stated denominator without treasury-stock offsets, and rerun per-share values at maximum payout.

audit_findings.title: Unrecognized tax liabilities may be an omitted claim on bridge cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $22.1 million filed at January 3, 2026, or $0.29 per stated diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: A cash settlement of an already accrued tax liability can reduce equity bridge cash without a matching future OE expense if it is not captured through working capital or another bridge adjustment.
audit_findings.evidence: The table of our material cash requirements above excludes unrecognized tax benefits as we are unable to reasonably predict the timing of settlement of liabilities, if any, related to unrecognized tax benefits.
audit_findings.explanation: The January liability is demonstrated, but its latest balance, settlement amount, and omission from the valuation are unresolved. Even a conservative dollar-for-dollar deduction of the full $22.1 million is only 1.3% of base equity value, reducing base value from $22.22 to about $21.93 per share and bull value from $26.07 to about $25.78, still well below the $40.82 price.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the July 4, 2026 unrecognized-tax-benefit balance and expected settlement, reconcile it to OE working-capital adjustments and bridge cash, and deduct only the portion not already captured.
